Grandma's Skillet Cornbread

The summer I turned nine, my grandmother kept a cast iron skillet on the back porch that nobody was allowed to touch. She had inherited it from her own mother, who carried it across three states in the bed of a pickup truck. Every Sunday she would haul it inside and the whole house would smell of butter and scorched corn. I have written about that porch before, and I will write about it again, because some kitchens never really leave you.

Anyway. Here is the recipe. Scroll past my nonsense if you like, I do not mind.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup stone-ground cornmeal
  • 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 1 cup buttermilk
  • 2 large eggs
  • 6 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees with the skillet inside.
  2. Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl.
  3. Beat the buttermilk and eggs together, then stir into the dry ingredients.
  4. Pour the batter into the hot skillet and bake 22 minutes, until the top is golden.

Tip: swap the buttermilk for plain kefir if that is what you have.
